title: AssemblyGrid v1: A Benchmark for Multi-Robot Production with Temporary Coalitions, Local Information, and Geometric Constraints
abstract: arXiv:2609.16075v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Flexible robotic production requires joint decisions on process progression, material routing, resource assignment, temporary cooperation, and simultaneous execution, since each decision can affect the feasibility of the others. The challenge is greater under decentralized control, where each robot acts from bounded local information while system progress depends on collective decisions, shared resources, material state, and workspace compatibility. These properties closely match cooperative multi-agent decision making under partial observability and resource contention. This paper introduces AssemblyGrid v1, a reproducible benchmark for repeated multi-robot production that combines explicit process progression, decentralized observations, material transfer, temporary multi-robot coalitions, productive concurrency, and geometry-dependent feasibility within one task-level formulation. The benchmark includes Flow, Coalition, and Concurre

translated_title: AssemblyGrid v1：一个具有临时联盟、局部信息和几何约束的多机器人生产基准测试
translated_abstract: 柔性机器人生产需要对工艺进程推进、物料路由、资源分配、临时协作和同步执行进行联合决策，因为每一项决策都可能影响其他决策的可行性。在分散式控制下，这一挑战更加严峻：每个机器人只能基于有限的局部信息行动，而系统的整体进度依赖于集体决策、共享资源、物料状态和工作空间兼容性。这些特性与部分可观测性和资源竞争条件下的协作式多智能体决策问题高度契合。本文提出了AssemblyGrid v1，这是一个可复现的多机器人重复生产基准测试，它在统一的任务级建模框架中结合了显式的工艺进程推进、分散式观测、物料传输、临时多机器人联盟、生产性并发以及依赖几何形状的任务可行性。该基准测试包含Flow、Coalition和Concurre（摘要在此处被截断，后续内容不完整）
tldr: 该论文提出了AssemblyGrid v1，这是一个将显式工艺进程、分散式局部观测、物料传输、临时多机器人联盟、生产性并发以及几何约束可行性统一整合到单一任务级框架中的可复现多机器人生产基准测试。
